title: Quoting a command line
description:
Build the single command-line string Windows passes to a new process, so the child gets the arguments back exactly.

```
["tool.exe", "a b", "plain", "say \"hi\"", "C:\\my dir\\"]
-> tool.exe "a b" plain "say \"hi\"" "C:\my dir\\"
```
hints: Walk the argument counting backslashes; when you reach a `"` (or the end, if quoting), write the backslashes twice before it (the rules from the Win32 API course, lesson 5.03, which lesson 1.02 builds on).
Never build a command line by adding quotes around each argument and hoping: an argument ending in `\` breaks that.
requirements: Arguments without spaces, tabs or quotes stay as they are; others are wrapped in quotes.
A `"` inside becomes `\"`; backslashes are doubled only when they come before a `"` (including the closing one).
Write a matching `split` that follows the same rules and check that every case comes back unchanged.
stretch: Explain why `CreateProcessW` needs the string to be writable.
